claims.text: Moderate wine consumption, particularly alongside meals, has been associated with lower cardiovascular mortality.
Moderate wine consumption, particularly alongside meals, has been associated with lower all-cause mortality.
Alcohol is an established carcinogen with evidence of increased cancer risk even at relatively low levels of consumption.
Moderation and synergy between lifestyle components may be more informative than the isolated attribution of health effects to individual foods or beverages.
The health associations attributed to moderate wine consumption may be inseparable from the broader Mediterranean lifestyle context in which it is embedded.

evidence.description: Moderate wine consumption, particularly alongside meals, has traditionally been incorporated into Mediterranean diet scores and has been associated with lower cardiovascular mortality.
Moderate wine consumption, particularly alongside meals, has traditionally been incorporated into Mediterranean diet scores and has been associated with lower all-cause mortality.
Alcohol is also an established carcinogen, with evidence of increased cancer risk even at relatively low levels of consumption.

Drawing on the concept of the traditional Mediterranean lifestyle, the authors propose that moderation and synergy between lifestyle components may be more informative than isolated attribution of health effects.
The authors hypothesize a 'hidden context' whereby health associations attributed to moderate wine consumption are inseparable from the broader Mediterranean lifestyle.

methodologies.name: Critical narrative synthesis
methodologies.description: Critical examination and conceptual synthesis of emerging evidence on wine consumption, Mediterranean dietary patterns, and methodological challenges in alcohol epidemiology.
conditions: Assessment of observational vs. Mendelian randomization evidence

limitations.text: Observational alcohol epidemiology is subject to abstainer-reference bias.
Observational alcohol epidemiology is vulnerable to reverse causation.
Observational alcohol epidemiology suffers from exposure misclassification.
There is a divergence between findings from observational studies and Mendelian randomization studies regarding alcohol consumption.

future_work.text: Evaluate the 'hidden context' hypothesis to investigate health associations of moderate wine consumption as inseparable from the broader Mediterranean lifestyle rather than searching for virtues in wine itself.
